A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ASF research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support matching retained material despite the shortened title, reformatted layout, and expanded appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original ASF detection results, computational measurements, ablations, sensor-failure examples, and feature visualizations, including additional quantitative results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds attention analyses, ten-seed statistics, stereo-encoder comparisons, and qualitative error cases in Appendices C and D.

M1.justification: Appendix D.2 adds an ASF variant that replaces monocular BEVDepth with stereo DSGN++, changing the camera encoder and its inputs. The core fusion procedure and SCL remain unchanged. Renaming CASAP-PN to CASAP does not remove post-feature normalization, which remains in Equations 7–8.

E1.justification: The limited coverage extension is the stereo-camera input scenario in v2 Table 8, beyond v1's implemented monocular camera branch. Both retain K-Radar benchmarks v1.0/v2.0, the same object classes, and weather/day-night coverage. The additional nighttime and adverse-weather illustrations do not establish new environmental coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 8 compares camera-only BEVDepth with DSGN++, alongside ASF using each encoder. Comparator membership in the retained accuracy and runtime comparisons is unchanged: RTNH, 3D-LRF, L4DR, and DPFT remain in their corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: v2 adds the stereo comparison at IoU=0.3, specifying sequences 1–20 for camera-only evaluation, and attention summaries using 8-meter distance bins. Appendix A.1 changes the stated training scope from only ASF components to ASF components plus the detection head; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. Existing benchmark regions, metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, t-SNE plots, and damaged-sensor examples, v2 adds weather- and distance-dependent attention analysis, stereo-backbone sensitivity, and random-seed robustness. Figures 7–8 also add detailed nighttime and adverse-weather error cases. These substantially broaden the questions investigated about ASF's behavior.

E5.justification: v1 reports no repeated-run counts or uncertainty estimates. v2 Table 7 first reports means and standard deviations over ten seeds, 0–8 and 2025, for ASF at IoU=0.3 across weather conditions. Appendix D also identifies seed 2025 for the retained Table 1 ASF results. This establishes new statistical reporting, not the number of runs previously performed.

E6.justification: v2 adds attention ratios, ten-seed summaries, stereo results, and qualitative failure findings. Table 8 reports camera-only Sedan AP3D of 17.8 for BEVDepth and 20.8 for DSGN++ under its stated evaluation. Table 2 changes DPFT speed from 10.8 to 11.5 FPS. Tables 1, 3, 4 and the original appendix Tables 5–8, now Tables 9–12, retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The complexity discussion changes SCF from O(N_s^2 N_p^2) to O(N_q N_s N_p), and ASF from O(N_s^2 N_p) to O(N_q N_s). This changes the mathematical scaling argument rather than merely notation. The method equations remain equivalent, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The main claims about availability-aware fusion, SCL, robustness, and the 9.7/20.1-percentage-point detection advantages are retained. The introduction and conclusion revise ASF's explicit computational-efficiency claim to O(N_q N_s), changing its stated scaling without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 substantially extends interpretation through explanations of distance-dependent sensor reliance, radar misses from overlapping reflections and road barriers, and weather-dependent seed variability. It also uses the stereo experiment to qualify the existing camera limitation: stronger camera-only detection yields little fusion benefit, attributed to LiDAR/radar dominance and the short stereo baseline.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code and log release; v2 states that these resources are available at the same repository. This is a change in reported access status, without external verification. Most existing implementation information, including hardware, optimizer, image and voxel sizes, and training duration, is retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 changes DPFT's characterization from computationally expensive fusion to reasonably efficient deformable attention, while retaining the representation-based distinction from ASF. v2 adds references for deformable attention and DSGN++ and removes v1 references 30, 31, and 37. The broader DCF/SCF positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the title, replaces CASAP-PN terminology with CASAP, adopts author-year citations, and condenses several experimental and ablation paragraphs. It inserts an attention-analysis appendix and moves the former Appendix C detection material to Appendix D. The main section order and most explanatory text are retained.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to predominantly one column with wrapped figures and tables. The first two figures exchange order, the Sedan t-SNE figure becomes a horizontal sequence, and captions and table headings are reformatted. Four new tables and two new figures are added; retained appendix tables are redistributed across pages containing references.

improvement.justification: The ten-seed statistics, attention analyses, and stereo/error studies provide useful additional evidence about stability and sensor limitations, while v2 reports code/log availability. The gains are bounded: uncertainty is reported at IoU=0.3 rather than the headline 0.5 threshold, the stereo discussion incorrectly gives Sedan AP3D as 24.8 instead of Table 8's 20.8, and the revised complexity claim leaves total patch-processing cost unclear. Overall, the added evidence improves the paper despite these reporting weaknesses.
